title: Property software firm emphasises client accounting compliance
summary:
Property management software provider Veco is focusing attention on client accounting systems as agencies face increasing compliance pressures. The company, which serves more than 2,000 UK agency branches, says accurate client account balances simplify audits and reduce regulatory risks.

title: 430,000 UK homeowners face £500+ monthly mortgage rises
summary:
More than 400,000 UK homeowners will face monthly mortgage payment increases exceeding £500 over the next three years, according to the Bank of England's financial policy committee. The analysis shows that of 7 million borrowers coming off fixed-rate deals before December 2029, approximately 6.5 million will face higher payments.

title: Lincolnshire records England’s highest damp property rates
summary:
Government data analysis reveals Lincolnshire dominates England's damp property statistics, with East Lindsey recording the highest rate at 13.4% of homes. Five Lincolnshire local authorities rank in the national top ten for properties affected by penetrating damp, rising damp and serious condensation.

title: UK housebuilding sector faces mounting challenges
summary:
The UK housebuilding sector is experiencing significant headwinds, with project delays and declining completions threatening government housing targets. Recent data reveals mounting pressures from regulatory requirements, high build costs, and weakening demand across multiple regions.

title: 64% of recent homebuyers consider interest-only mortgages
summary:
Almost two-thirds of homeowners who purchased property within the past five years would consider switching to interest-only mortgage payments as borrowing costs rise. A survey of 910 recent homebuyers found that 64% would consider moving to interest-only repayments, while 73% expressed concern about higher mortgage costs when remortgaging.

title: Estate agents expect AI to reshape compliance within two years
summary:
86% of senior compliance leaders at property firms expect AI to play a significant role in their compliance function within two years, according to Thirdfort research.

title: AI phone system handles tenant repairs for housing providers
summary:
A UK-based AI phone receptionist service has launched an out-of-hours line for housing associations and councils to handle tenant repair calls and fly-tipping reports. The system answers calls immediately, provides safety advice, and forwards reports to on-call teams within seconds.

title: Tribunals reduce landlord rent increases by 40% on average
summary:
First-Tier Tribunals have approved rent increases in approximately two-thirds of cases since the Renters' Rights Act came into effect, but at rates 40% below landlords' requests. Data shows landlords requested average increases of 9.8% but received approval for 5.8% rises.

title: Estate agents require most Google reviews for ChatGPT listing
summary:
Estate agents require significantly more Google reviews than other trades to receive recommendations from ChatGPT, according to research conducted by Wigan-based digital agency Mako Digital. The typical estate agent recommended by ChatGPT had accumulated 529 Google reviews, the highest threshold among eight trades examined.

title: Half of UK letting agencies fail to publish accurate fees
summary:
Over half of letting agencies in the UK are failing to comply with legal requirements to publish accurate fee information online, according to new research. A review of 2,818 letting agencies found that 51% are displaying outdated information on their websites, whilst 19% do not publish their landlord fees online at all.
